ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is dark indigo to black with a bright yellow snout and limbs. It features a granular dorsum and distinct white spots on the flanks. It lacks vomerine teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes indigo* is uniquely distinguished by its vibrant, deep indigo-blue coloration on the hidden surfaces of its groin and thighs, unlike the paler hues of relatives.
ai.habitat: The Indigo Bush Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indigo Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden within dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes indigo* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes indigo* is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests of the southern Western Ghats, specifically in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The Indigo Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like "tseep" call, typically heard as a series of rapid, repetitive notes from within dense rainforest vegetation.
